title: Low Oil Prices Challenge China’s Fight Against Pollution

image.attribution: NASA/GSFC, MODIS Rapid Response / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
The low price of oil has saved China billions of dollars on imports. But energy analysts and industry experts say it is also creating challenges for China’s leaders who have committed themselves to cleaning up the environment.

China has pledged to take steps to reduce its carbon footprint to improve its sullied image as one of the world’s worst emitters of greenhouse gases. Its determination to fulfill the pledge will be closely watched at the United Nations climate change talks in Paris later this year.

In recent years, China has adopted a range of strategies to reduce its use of oil by building additional capacities in sectors such as natural gas, hydroelectric, nuclear, solar and wind power. But the higher price of oil and the need for a clean environment were key drivers of such initiatives.

China has seen a massive surge in imports and its reserves have bulged. Last month, the country surpassed the United States as the world’s biggest importer of oil for the first time.

Earlier this week, Chinese President Xi Jinping said the increase in imports was essential to China’s efforts to build up a complete contingency safety plan for oil reserves.

Crude oil contributes 19 percent in the country’s energy mix, natural gas accounts for six percent, while coal is still the biggest contributor meeting 64 percent of China’s energy requirements.

questions.question: Why is the low price of oil creating challenges for China?
options: It limits the drive for alternative energy sources.
It increases dependency on imported oil.
It causes economic growth to stagnate.
It undermines commitments to environmental initiatives.
questions.answer: It undermines commitments to environmental initiatives.

questions.question: Who will watch China’s progress in reducing greenhouse gas emissions?
options: The United Nations climate change conference attendees.
questions.answer: The United Nations climate change conference attendees.

questions.question: How is China trying to reduce its use of oil?
options: By decreasing its natural gas imports.
By investing in various alternative energy sources.
By reducing energy consumption across all sectors.
By increasing its reliance on coal energy.
questions.answer: By investing in various alternative energy sources.
